summary: Tested Bybit housekeeping (weekly re-optimisation + automatic pruning) end-to-end. Backend: new pytest suite tests/test_iter75_housekeeping.py, 10/10 passing. It covers the settings defaults and validation (an invalid reopt symbol is dropped, auto_prune_pf=2 and min_trades=1 return 422), that FX/Pepperstone settings have none of the new keys and their /housekeeping routes return 404, the shape of GET /api/housekeeping, and the full live prune flow with seeded trades: <=10 trades never warned; 12 trades with PF 0.2 warned; an immediate repeat does nothing; a warning backdated 21 h switches the pair off and removes it from symbols, with an auto_prune evolution event; an inactive pair is left alone; after re-adding the pair and replacing its trades with winners it is 'cleared'. Unit tests with a fake engine and patched optimize/notify cover: params applied only when robust>0 and actually different (20 vs 20.0 does not update), 'ha pasado a ser RENTABLE' sent only for a profitable switched-off pair, the _profitable thresholds at their exact limits, and tick skipping when checked <300 s ago or nothing is due (and running both jobs when due). POST /api/housekeeping/reopt live returned 200 with results for ZEC (profitable, PF 1.1, robust 1.117, params unchanged so nothing applied) and HYPE (robust -0.39, not applied, not profitable). Frontend /bybit: in the 'Pares 30d' tab maintenance-status shows ZEC 'rentable' and HYPE 'no rentable' rows and prune-warned reads 'Ningún par en aviso.'. prune-run-button shows the toast 'Ningún par cumple el criterio de poda'. Both switches are checked, the ZEC/HYPE chips are highlighted, the inputs show 0.8 and 10, and toggling the HYPE chip off, saving and reloading persisted ['ZECUSDT'], then toggling it back on restored ['ZECUSDT','HYPEUSDT']. /hotforex has none of the new elements.

minor.issue: The optimizer took ~2 s here, much faster than the expected 60-90 s, because klines are cached for 300 s. So I ran it twice by accident, and could not produce the 409 'already running' case by timing; the lock check was only read in code.

issues: The pair-ranking/maintenance card takes about 2/3 of the width and leaves a large empty dark area to its right (existing layout, minor)

action_items: Optional: prune() only ranks settings.symbols plus pairs that have trades. A warned pair that is switched off manually and has no trades in 30 days keeps its stale meta.prune.warned entry; also clear warned entries for symbols not in settings.symbols.

Optional: when all bad pairs would remove the last symbol, off is reset to [] but their warned entries were already popped. They get re-warned next day instead of staying warned, so the Telegram warning repeats daily.
Optional: manual POST /housekeeping/prune ignores auto_prune_enabled and resets meta.prune.last_at, which delays the daily automatic run. Document this or respect the flag.
critical_code_review_comments: housekeeping.py is clean and small. The float-normalised compare is correct, and the lock is shared by the API and tick.
reopt_symbols validator silently drops invalid entries and caps at 6. An empty list is allowed (the endpoint returns 400 then). OK.
Turning the bot's own pairs off is risky and is only guarded by the 20 h window. Notify returns False when Telegram is unconfigured, so a user without Telegram gets no warning before the switch-off.
